internal: Why now. On the Aug 13 2026 call Maximus credited a 15.0% adjusted EBITDA margin to productivity gains across core programs and put a number on front-office AI (IVR, chatbot, proactive engagement): a 3.5% operating-margin lift on five contracts. No back-office figure was given. Three AI executives arrived in April and May 2026.

The gap. Verint Operations Visualizer and Operations Productivity, 1,510 seats (3xG sheet), is a monitoring layer on case-processing work. Nothing public shows rules-based reallocation of people or work behind it, while the business runs on contract-driven volume swings (Medicaid unwinding, VA exam volume, UI backlogs).

The pressure. The VA paused Medical Disability Exam incentives on Jul 1 2026 while it rebuilds invoice validation; that alone cut FY2026 EPS guidance about $0.35 and pushed revenue guidance to the low end. Timeliness and accuracy reporting on a flagship program is under the customer's microscope.

Gate. Not a current Intradiem customer or partner (Salesforce segment Sep 1 2026), not registered by any partner in the pre-pipeline. Clear to work. The enterprise WFM owner Jeremy's brief could not confirm is Marc Hillman, Senior Director of Workforce Management, found on the free Clay path.
partner: Why now. On the Aug 13 2026 call Maximus credited its margin to productivity gains across core programs and quantified front-office AI work on five contracts. Back-office case processing was not part of that story. Three AI executives arrived in April and May 2026.

Where the conversation sits. Case-processing work (eligibility, claims, appeals, clinical exam administration) swings with contract volume. Real-time orchestration of that work and the people doing it is the layer that sits beside the desktop analytics Maximus already runs.

h2_findings: A services business whose margin now depends on productivity, with the back office left out of its own automation story.

items.t: About 37,200 employees plus 9,300 contingent workers at Sep 30 2025: 15,000 U.S. Federal Services, 13,600 U.S. Services, 6,900 Outside the U.S., 1,700 corporate. Segment split read through search extraction of the 10-K; re-check against the filing before external use.

Case-processing functions on the record: Medicaid and CHIP eligibility and enrollment, unemployment insurance claims and appeals (California EDD backlog engagement), clinical and functional disability assessments (VA MDE, UK DWP), federal student loan servicing (Aidvantage).

Contact-center side: 1-800-MEDICARE and Federal Marketplace under the CMS Contact Center Operations contract (base plus nine option years, $6.6B ceiling), CDC-INFO, IRS citizen services (70,000+ calls a day cited).
Verint Operations Visualizer and Operations Productivity, 1,510 seats, sold direct. Desktop activity tracking on case-processing work. Not confirmed in any public source; treat as internal.

Back-office population: a planning band of 20,000 to 25,000 FTEs touching case-processing work, from the segment split above (U.S. Services and the UK assessment business skew to processing; Federal mixes live-queue and exam administration). Our math, not a company figure.
Delivery footprint: Tysons VA headquarters; Victoria BC, Bengaluru, Riyadh, the Emirates, London listed. No published site count or onshore-offshore split for processing work.

sections.title: Segments, contracts and restructuring, last 24 months

items.t: FY2025 revenue $5.43B: U.S. Federal Services $3.07B (+12.1%), U.S. Services $1.76B (-7.7%, Medicaid unwinding volume rolling off), Outside the U.S. $600M (-8.7%).
Australia and South Korea employment-services businesses sold in Q1 FY2025 (about $38M in divestiture charges), framed as margin-accretive.

CMS CCO contract: the 2024 re-procurement was protested, GAO partially sustained on Sep 16 2024, CMS cancelled the solicitation and Maximus continues under the existing contract into its option years.
VA Medical Disability Exam program: the VA paused performance incentives and disincentives effective Jul 1 2026 while it revamps invoice review and validation.
A new Medicaid redetermination wave is expected in 2026 under the work-requirement provisions of the 2025 reconciliation law; Maximus has not quantified its own volume from it.
Over 60% of H1 FY2025 revenue on performance-based or fixed-price federal contracts; analysts framed Maximus as relatively insulated from 2025 stop-work orders.

sections.title: Cost pressure and the productivity story

items.t: Q3 FY2026 (Aug 13 2026): revenue $1.28B, adjusted EPS $2.22, adjusted EBITDA margin 15.0% (from 14.7%), attributed to productivity gains across core program areas. FY2026 revenue guidance $5.2B to $5.35B, leaning to the low end; adjusted EPS guidance cut about $0.35 for the VA incentive pause.

Same call: 75 to 80% of new bids and rebids now carry explicit AI requirements or evaluation criteria; AI work on five contracts (IVR optimization, chatbot enhancement, proactive engagement) produced a cited 3.5% operating-margin improvement. Front-office examples only.
Q3 FY2026: adjusted EBITDA margin 15.0%, up from 14.7%, credited to productivity gains; full-year guidance leaning to the low end after the VA incentive pause.
FY2025: operating margin 9.7%, adjusted EBITDA margin 12.9%, free cash flow $366M. FY2026 initial guide: adjusted EBITDA margin about 13.7%.
Revenue per employee about $146,000 on 37,200 employees, or about $117,000 including contingent workers.
Maximus Ventures invested in Spectro Cloud (AI infrastructure for secure government deployment) in the Q3 FY2026 window.
The VA's incentive pause is a customer rebuilding how it validates timeliness and accuracy on a flagship program; the reporting behind exam throughput is under scrutiny now.

Maximus markets backlog clearing as a strength: a 5.7 million-task UI backlog, 3.6 million claims in eight months, a 3,000-person workforce stood up in six months. Large, spiky processing queues that need fast reallocation are the business.

Prior state corrective actions on call abandonment, answer times, backlogs and missed 60-day application timeframes (a state DHS engagement, the Kansas Clearinghouse contract), all pre-2025. Pattern evidence, not current.
Texas HHS OIG audit of Maximus as Medicaid and CHIP enrollment broker exists; the PDF returned 403 on fetch and is unread.
Open eligibility roles ask for accurate and timely benefit determinations in complex eligibility operations; standard requisition language, not distress.

Glassdoor 3.2 of 5 across 6,100+ reviews; recurring themes are understaffed projects, tight deadlines, refusal to backfill, and contract-cycle staffing swings (one review cites a 75% workforce cut on a contract at year end).

Amazon Connect in active use: a UK Amazon Connect Developer posting asks for migration experience from Five9 and Liberty Netcall, which reads as a platform move in progress in at least the UK operation.

AI leadership from LinkedIn (Clay free path): Kathleen Featheringham, SVP AI (Apr 2026); Daniel Biernacki, SVP AI Transformation and Experience (May 2026); Lauren Donovan, Senior Director AI Transformation and Experience (May 2026). Derrick Pledger has been Chief Digital and Information Officer since Jan 2024.

Workforce management layer from LinkedIn (Clay free path): Marc Hillman, Senior Director of Workforce Management (Feb 2022); Drex Fitzwater, VP Strategic Workforce Planning; Dave Harkess, VP Contact Center Operations; Michael Koodin, Project Manager Strategic Workforce Analytics (Mar 2026).
RPA vendor, CRM or case-management platform, and cloud provider: none named in public sources this pass. A VP Cloud Technology (Chris Ray, 100+ staff) confirms a cloud practice.

Maturity read: front-office automation is real and quantified by the company; back-office automation is undocumented in public and the only concrete back-office technology signal is a monitoring layer. Visibility without orchestration.

h2_say: What we can put in writing.

we_can_say.t: Intradiem sits between the ACD and WFM. It is not a WFM replacement; Verint, NICE and Calabrio are the layer it acts on top of.
Dynamic Workforce Orchestration: continuously sensing demand, reallocating work, and supporting employees as conditions shift through the day, in the idle seconds between scheduled activities.
Net retention above 114% in 2025; record net new bookings in 2025; customer savings at an all-time high for full-year 2025.
About 350,000 contact center professionals on platform.
A healthcare customer reported 4.5X annualized ROI in the first quarter of operations; another saved 1,700 hours of agent off-phone time.
we_can_say.s: Value Repository, intradiem.com, blinded unless logo-approved

scenario_note: The 3xG brief models $9.75M to $29.25M in annual savings from a $65,000 fully loaded FTE cost times 10, 20 or 30% of the 1,500 Verint seats. Seats on a 2024 licensing sheet are not back-office FTEs, the lift percentages are assumptions, and none of it is in the Value Repository. It stays out of anything a partner seller or Maximus sees. The business case comes from discovery data through the ROI skill after the 40-minute meeting.
h2_questions: Five questions that come from the record, not the pitch.

questions.q: The Q3 call put a 3.5% margin lift on AI work across five contracts. Is that measured on the contact-center side only, or does it reach the eligibility, claims and appeals queues behind the same contracts?

With the VA pausing exam incentives while it rebuilds invoice validation, how much of your throughput and timeliness reporting comes from real-time operational data versus after-the-fact reconciliation?
As unwinding volume normalizes and a new redetermination wave phases in, how do you move people across eligibility, appeals and 1-800-MEDICARE queues when volume shifts week to week?

You've got a desktop analytics layer on a large part of the processing workforce. Is that data driving any rules-based reallocation of idle or surge capacity today, or is it a monitoring and reporting layer?
questions.from: 3xG seat data; ask as understanding their environment, never as citing it

questions.q: With 75 to 80% of new federal bids carrying AI criteria, how are you positioning the back-office side of proposals, eligibility and document review, next to the contact-center automation story on the calls?
